notes: Publication-safe: no internal names, ids or paths. Internal provenance for every figure is in the brief (announcement_brief.md), which stays in the research repo.

Every figure with standin=true was measured on the current development model or an earlier internal model, as its measured_on says. They are realistic stand-ins and will be re-measured for the release.
Lower is better for regret metrics; coverage is best when it equals its nominal level (0.50, 0.80, 0.95).
Baselines: 'Bayesian optimisation (GP)' = Gaussian-process Thompson sampling (BoTorch); 'TabPFN v2.5' = Prior Labs' TabPFN v2.5 regressor used as the surrogate with expected improvement.

model.name: [MODEL NAME]
model.one_line: A foundation model for experiment design: it reads a campaign's results so far and proposes which experiments to run next.

model_details.type: Prior-fitted transformer (meta-learned Bayesian predictor and proposer)
model_details.architecture: Transformer that attends across the experiments run so far and across their input parameters; 6 layers, width 256, 8 heads
model_details.inputs: The campaign so far: parameter settings and measured outcomes, plus declared outcome limits (a floor where runs fail, a ceiling where a readout saturates)
outputs: A full predictive distribution of the outcome at any untested setting (1000-bin histogram, so skewed, multi-modal and bounded outcomes are represented)
The probability that a run succeeds
Proposals for the next experiment or batch of experiments

training_data.summary: Synthetic only. About 9.6 million simulated optimisation campaigns drawn from a designed prior. No real or customer data was used for training, fine-tuning or calibration.
task_families: Landscapes with localised peaks, including needle-like optima
Random neural-network functions (abrupt and interacting effects)
Structural variants of these: only a few parameters mattering, categorical inputs, step changes, regime switches, skewed outcomes, input-dependent noise, infeasible regions
variation_in_training: 1 to 100 parameters per problem, weighted toward small problems (about two thirds of tasks have 20 or fewer)
Noise levels from near-exact to very noisy, replicate measurements
Batch effects and hidden factors that change outcomes between runs
Failed runs and saturated readouts (outcomes recorded only within limits)
Histories of up to 60 measured experiments, collected by several search strategies

intended_use: Choosing the next experiments in lab campaigns where each experiment is expensive: formulation, media and buffer optimisation, assay development, protocol and process parameters
Ranking a candidate list (for example a plate of untested formulations) by expected outcome and uncertainty
Campaigns that aim for a target value, stay within limits, or trade off several outcomes
out_of_scope: Safety-critical decisions without expert review (for example clinical dosing)
Problems with more parameters than the operating envelope below
Replacing domain knowledge about what is safe or feasible to run

operating_envelope.history_length_trained: up to 60 experiments (works beyond, with gradually wider intervals)
operating_envelope.batch_proposals: yes, one experiment to a full plate per round
operating_envelope.time_per_proposal: about 8 seconds on a CPU (up to about 20)

model_card.evaluation_summary: Held-out synthetic functions through the same interface labs use, public hyperparameter-optimisation benchmarks (HPO-B, PD1) and a published cell-free protein expression dataset. None of these were used in training.

headline_candidates.text_template: On landscapes with narrow optima and abrupt changes it found better results than standard Bayesian optimisation in {wins} of {runs} campaigns.
Beat random search in {pct} of {runs} held-out campaigns.
When it gives a 95% range, the measured result lands inside it {cov95} of the time; a fitted Gaussian process, {gp_cov95}.
Finds half of the best 5% of formulations {factor}x faster than random screening.
headline_candidates.not_measured_yet: Measured so far only for standard Bayesian optimisation (2.6x to 4.5x). The model's own figure is pending.

benchmarks.title: Search efficiency on held-out problems
benchmarks.question: How close to the best possible result does each method get within 50 experiments?
benchmarks.task: Optimise 11 held-out test functions (not in training), run through the same interface a lab uses: 50 experiments in batches of 5.

dataset.name: Standard optimisation test functions (Branin, Hartmann 3 and 6, Ackley, Holder table, Michalewicz, Shekel, Voronoi)
dataset.citation: Surjanovic and Bingham, Virtual Library of Simulation Experiments

baselines.name: Bayesian optimisation (GP)
baselines.settings: Gaussian process, Thompson sampling, same initial design

baselines.name: TabPFN v2.5
baselines.settings: TabPFN v2.5 regressor, expected improvement, same initial design

metric.name: Final regret relative to random search (mean final regret per problem divided by random's, averaged over problems)

benchmarks.runs: 10 seeds per problem; groups: smooth (6 problems, 60 runs), narrow optima or abrupt changes (4 problems, 40 runs), Ackley (1 problem, 10 runs)
benchmarks.spread: Paired per seed (same seeds and initial designs for every method); win counts above.
benchmarks.scope: Synthetic test functions with 2 to 6 parameters; noise-free and high-noise variants of the smooth problems.
caveats: Standard Bayesian optimisation is better on smooth problems, where its assumptions hold.
The TabPFN arm ran on the identical seeds four days earlier, on slightly older code.

benchmarks.title: Can you trust its uncertainty?
benchmarks.question: When the model gives an 80% or 95% range, how often does the measured value land inside?
benchmarks.task: Predict held-out outcomes from campaign histories of the held-out problems, with and without a failure floor (the worst half of outcomes recorded only as 'failed').

metric.name: Interval coverage at nominal 50% / 80% / 95%
metric.unit: share of outcomes inside the interval

results.group: Half of outcomes below a failure floor

benchmarks.spread: Pooled over 660 cases; PIT KS (lower is better): model 0.14, GP 0.18 without floor; 0.21 vs 0.25 with floor.
caveats: Under a large failure floor every model tested is over-confident; improving this is active work.

benchmarks.title: Ranking untested settings on public benchmarks
benchmarks.question: Given n tested settings, how well does each model rank the untested ones?
benchmarks.task: Rank every untested configuration of real hyperparameter-optimisation search spaces from n observed ones.

dataset.name: HPO-B (v3 test split) and PD1
dataset.citation: Pineda Arango et al., HPO-B, NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks 2021; Wang et al., Pre-trained Gaussian processes for Bayesian optimization (PD1), JMLR 2024

metric.name: Median Spearman rank correlation, predicted vs true, over untested settings

benchmarks.runs: Paired cells per n (task x seed x history)
benchmarks.spread: Median over paired cells; TabPFN ahead on 73 to 90% of cells from 25 points.
benchmarks.scope: Hyperparameter tuning surfaces (machine learning), not lab data; many tied plateau values.
caveats: TabPFN ranks better here, especially on HPO-B. The model's 95% intervals hold (coverage 0.95 to 0.98).

benchmarks.title: Search on HPO-B
benchmarks.question: How quickly does each method find good configurations on a public benchmark?
benchmarks.task: Bayesian-optimisation runs on HPO-B tasks with up to 6 parameters, 5 fixed initial designs each, one experiment at a time.

dataset.name: HPO-B v3 test split
dataset.citation: Pineda Arango et al., NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks 2021

baselines.name: Bayesian optimisation (GP)
baselines.settings: Thompson sampling (ours) and HPO-B's published GP

baselines.name: FSBO (published)
baselines.settings: transfer-trained on HPO-B's own training tasks

benchmarks.spread: Against the published GP: better in 45, worse in 42 of the decided cells (not significant).
caveats: FSBO is trained on HPO-B's own training tasks; ours never saw HPO-B.
The model leads early and is overtaken by TabPFN by 100 evaluations.

benchmarks.title: Real lab data: cell-free protein expression
benchmarks.question: Given some measured formulations, which untested ones should be made next?
benchmarks.task: Rerank the untested formulations of a published three-stage cell-free reagent campaign from k measured ones.

dataset.name: Cell-free reagent formulations (three stages, 13 / 28 / 21 reagents, 1,231 formulations)

metric.name: Top-5% recall of the next picks, and 80% interval coverage

benchmarks.runs: 30 random contexts per k, three stages

paired.comparison: model vs TabPFN v2.5, better single next pick

benchmarks.spread: Recall differences under 0.05 are within noise.
benchmarks.scope: One published campaign; random contexts. Replaying the lab's own round order, every model is over-confident and the last stage is barely better than random.
caveats: Top-pick quality is level with TabPFN; the clear difference is calibration.

benchmarks.title: Experiments saved
benchmarks.question: How many fewer experiments to find the best formulations than random screening?
benchmarks.task: Search each cell-free stage for its top 5% / top 1% formulations, 200 experiments, one at a time.

metric.name: Acceleration factor: random's median experiments to the goal divided by the method's

caveats: The model's own figures are not measured yet.

capabilities.name: Batches
capabilities.text: Proposes a whole batch at once, from a single experiment to a full plate.

capabilities.name: Targets, not just maxima
capabilities.text: Aim for a value (for example 50% yield within a tolerance) and get the probability of landing in range.
capabilities.evidence: Native targets beat rewriting the goal as 'maximise minus distance' in 41 to 48 of 60 paired runs per method (earlier internal model).

capabilities.name: Failed runs and saturated readouts
capabilities.text: Declare where runs fail or a readout saturates; the model treats those outcomes as censored rather than exact.

capabilities.name: Limits on other outcomes
capabilities.text: Keep cost, purity or other measured outcomes within limits while optimising one.

capabilities.name: Several objectives
capabilities.text: Map the trade-off front between competing outcomes.

capabilities.name: Mixed parameter types
capabilities.text: Continuous, integer, log-scale, categorical parameters and mixtures that must sum to a total.

capabilities.name: No per-campaign tuning
capabilities.text: Nothing is fitted or tuned per campaign: the model reads the history and predicts directly.

limitations: On smooth, well-behaved problems standard Bayesian optimisation is as good or better.
On public hyperparameter benchmarks TabPFN ranks untested settings better, increasingly so with more data.
When a large share of runs fail, every model tested (this one included) is over-confident.
In multi-objective mode it trails both baselines, and it gains least from declared limits on other outcomes (earlier internal model).
Trained only on synthetic campaigns: some structured response families outside its training prior are predicted less well than by a Gaussian process or TabPFN.
Histories longer than 60 experiments are outside training; predictions still work, with wider intervals.
